subject: AuroraSys — Processing locations, subprocessors, and erase commitments
messages:
From: Emma Li <emma.li@aurorasys.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@aurorasys.com
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Processing footprint and erase commitments for AuroraSys evaluation

Hi Olga,

Thanks for taking the call yesterday. As we kick off the security review for AuroraSys, procurement and security need a concise picture of where Redwood processes customer inference requests, which subprocessors are involved, and the concrete commitments around data deletion/erase for transient request data.

Can you confirm:
- Primary regions where inference executes for the hosted service (and options to restrict to US-only).
- Any third-party subprocessors that may see request payloads or logs (names + country).
- Typical retention for request payloads, logs, and KV cache snapshots, and how a customer-triggered erase is enacted (time-to-complete and evidence artifacts).

We aim to close this round of vendor due diligence by next Friday. If you can send a short evidence package and a pointer to any SOC2/arch docs, that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Emma Li
Security Program Manager — AuroraSys
emma.li@aurorasys.com

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@aurorasys.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Processing footprint and erase commitments for AuroraSys evaluation

Hi Emma — great to be working with AuroraSys on this. Below is a concise, operational summary; I'll attach a compact evidence bundle (subprocessor matrix + redacted flow diagrams) in a follow-up.

1) Execution regions- Hosted API default: multi-region routing (us-central + us-west) to optimize latency. Customers can request region pinning to US-only (controls in account settings or via support ticket for enterprise contracts). For Dedicated/Private deployments, execution occurs only in customer-specified regions or on-premise.

2) Subprocessors that may touch inference traffic- Redwood Core runtime (self-hosted by Redwood in our cloud regions) — Redwood-managed (US).- CDN/edge TLS termination providers (for streaming responses) — located in US/EU; we can restrict endpoints to US-only for export-controlled customers.- Logging/telemetry pipeline: aggregated logs are written to our telemetry cluster; raw request payloads are not stored by default except when customers opt in for debug logging or when we capture minimal telemetry during errors.

3) Retention and erase process- Default: transient request data is ephemeral — kept only in memory + GPU KV cache for the request lifecycle. Minimal non-identifying request metadata (timestamps, routing IDs) are stored in logs for 7 days by default for debugging and billing reconciliation.- If a customer requests erase: we initiate an account-scoped purge that removes stored logs/metadata and cycles any persisted diagnostic blobs. For hosted customers, most erases complete within 48 hours; for any records in external analytics or long-term stores, we coordinate deletion with the subprocessors (typical SLA 7–14 days depending on legal/backup windows).- We provide an erase attestment (signed PDF) and a short deletion summary exported as a Drive link or HubSpot record upon completion.

I'm attaching a short matrix of subprocessors and a redacted evidence zip. Connor is looping on SLA specifics and will follow with the subprocessor contact list for AuroraSys.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: redwood_subprocessor_matrix_20270427.pdf; data_residency_evidence_bundle.zip

From: Carlos Mendez <c.mendez@aurorasys.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Emma Li <emma.li@aurorasys.com>, procurement@aurorasys.com, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Processing footprint and erase commitments for AuroraSys evaluation

Olga —

Thanks for the overview. Two clarifications so we can map to our vendor risk matrix:
1) When you say "minimal non-identifying request metadata" is stored for 7 days, can you enumerate the exact fields (e.g., request ID, timestamp, model_id, token_count, originating IP)? We need to know if any IPs or customer identifiers are retained.
2) For the erase attestment, can you confirm the precise contents (what the PDF contains) and whether that includes audit-trail hashes for deleted objects? Our legal team requires a small audit trail showing the deletion action and the artifacts removed.

Also, we have a procurement constraint: any subprocessor in the EU or APAC requires additional export-control review. Could you provide country-of-operation for each subprocessor in your matrix?

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Carlos Mendez
Head of Procurement — AuroraSys
procurement@aurorasys.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Carlos Mendez <c.mendez@aurorasys.com>, Emma Li <emma.li@aurorasys.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Processing footprint and erase commitments for AuroraSys evaluation

Hi Carlos / Emma — quick answers inline and attached a short CSV with country-of-operation for each listed subprocessor.

1) Stored fields (7-day debug/billing logs): request_id (GUID), timestamp (UTC), model_id (string), token_count (integer), routing_region (enum). We do NOT store full request payloads or customer-submitted PII in the default telemetry stream. Originating IP is captured only transiently for rate-limiting and is redacted in logs after 24 hours.

2) Erase attestment contents: date/time of request, account ID, list of logical buckets scoped to the purge (e.g., "billing-logs-2027-04"), confirmation of subprocessor deletion coordination steps, and a deletion reference ID. We also include a SHA256 hash of the deletion manifest (not of deleted user content) so customers can verify the artifact integrity. The attestment is signed by Redwood Security and includes the slate of subprocessors contacted.

Attachment stubs: redwood_subprocessor_matrix_20270427.pdf (with country column); data_residency_evidence_bundle.zip (redacted flow diagrams + SOC2 summary).

Connor will follow up with any enterprise-only opt-in controls (audit log retention windows and contract addenda).

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Emma Li <emma.li@aurorasys.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Carlos Mendez <c.mendez@aurorasys.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 11:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Processing footprint and erase commitments for AuroraSys evaluation

Marissa / Olga —

Appreciate the detail. The CSV and attestment description look like exactly what legal and procurement need. Two quick asks before we close:
- Can you confirm the erase SLA in a single sentence we can paste into our vendor sheet (e.g., "Redwood will complete account-scoped log and metadata purges within 48 hours; subprocessor deletions coordinated within 14 days").
- Could you point us to the SOC2 public page or provide a copy of the latest SOC2 Type II?

If you can send those two items and the Drive link to the evidence bundle, we'll move this to approval.

Best,
Emma
